findings.title: U.S. seeks to extradite Saskatoon man accused of hacking educational systems to mine crypto
findings.summary_md: The United States sought extradition of Ryan James Roach, a Saskatoon man accused of hacking into American university systems to illegally use their supercomputers for cryptocurrency mining. Roach faced conspiracy to commit unauthorized use of a computer, punishable by up to ten years in prison in Canada, and maintained his innocence through his lawyer. One undisclosed U.S. educational institution suffered about 337000 US dollars in damages from system shutdowns, forensic analysis, and rebuilding compromised infrastructure. A Saskatchewan judge had to decide whether the U.S. evidence met Canada's extradition test.

findings.title: Sask. man ordered for extradition to U.S. over university hacking for crypto mining
findings.summary_md: A Saskatchewan King's Bench judge ordered Ryan James Roach extradited to the United States to face charges related to hacking into American university supercomputers to mine cryptocurrency. The judge found the evidence against Roach met Canada's legal threshold for extradition while stressing the ruling does not determine innocence or guilt. The province's Court of Appeal subsequently granted Roach interim release pending a final decision by the federal justice minister.

findings.title: Canadian man extradited to the U.S. for his role in computer hacking scheme targeting universities
findings.summary_md: A federal grand jury in Rochester, New York indicted Ryan James Roach of Saskatchewan and Mathiew James Stubbings of Ontario on conspiracy and computer damage charges tied to a campaign running from June 2016 through December 2019. The defendants allegedly used virtual private servers registered under fraudulent identities to deliver malware and mining software to victim computers and store stolen login credentials. Universities in New York, Massachusetts, North Carolina, and Tennessee were compromised, with a focus on campuses running supercomputers. Roach was extradited from Canada on October 28, 2026 and arraigned on November 3, while extradition proceedings against Stubbings continue.
